Do you have any idea how game hacking works?

Most of the "hacks" that actually get used are simple graphical overlays that take advantage of client-side data storage built into the multiplayer itself. Stuff like that only really requires a single dll hook to work and the only effective countermeasure is a damn good anti-hack system. Any decent anti-hack system relies on automatic detection to function. On a brand new game all the hacks are brand new, so they'll be a hell of a lot of hacks that slip by early on because the anti-cheat service hasn't had enough time to figure out what is and isn't a cheat yet.

If you were paying attention you would have seen that the same thing happened in BF4. A surge of hacks within a month or so of release, then nothing for six months, then a slow trickling of hacks as hackers got more creative about circumventing the antihack system.

With relatively ineffective anti-cheat services such as PB or FF, this is more or less how it will always happen, and DICE isn't going to abandon PB or FF anytime soon.
